name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 356 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 16% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 356 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 16 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Security forces in Chhattisgarh uncovered a major Maoist weapons cache in Sukma, seizing two IEDs and explosives, while LG Manoj Sinha chaired high-level security meetings in both Kashmir and the Kashmir division, directing sustained action against terror modules and tightening counter-infiltration grids. In Manipur, a shutdown began in a district after two Kuki youths went missing, the state announced ex-gratia for families of 32 Kuki-Zo civilians killed, and a former chief minister accused BJP leaders of orchestrating his ouster and ongoing violence. The Mirwaiz of Kashmir called for the release of political prisoners and restoration of civil liberties, urging justice and trust rebuilding. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrker i Chhattisgarh avdekket en stor maoistisk våpenlager i Sukma, og beslagla to IED-er og sprengstoff, mens LG Manoj Sinha ledet høytstående sikkerhetsmøter både i Kashmir og i Kashmir-divisjonen, og ga ordre om vedvarende aksjon mot terrormoduler og tettere grensekontroller mot infiltrasjon. I Manipur startet en nedstengning i en distrikts etter at to Kuki-ungdom forsvant, staten kunngjorde eks-gratias til familiene til 32 Kuki-Zo-sivilister som ble drept, og en tidligere statsminister anklaget BJP-ledere for å ha orkestrert hans avsettelse og den pågående volden. Mirwaiz i Kashmir ba om løslatelse av politiske fanger og gjenoppretting av sivile friheter, og oppfordret til rettferdighet og gjenoppbygging av tillit. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
